title: Flexbox basics
summary: Lay out children in a row or a column with display: flex, and let them share the space.

quiz.q: Which element do you give `display: flex` to?
quiz.explain: Flexbox is switched on in the container. Its direct children become flex items and are laid out along a line.
The default is `row`. `column` places the items top to bottom.

quiz.q: Three flex items each have `flex: 1`. What happens?
options: They share the free space equally
quiz.explain: `flex: 1` means grow to take an equal share of the leftover space.

quiz.q:
The HTML is `

A

B

`. The author wants A and B side by side, but they stack. Click the faulty line.
quiz.explain: `display: flex` belongs on the parent (`.row`), not on the items. Putting it on the items only changes how their own contents are laid out.

quiz.q: In a row flex container, which direction is the **main axis**?
quiz.explain: For `flex-direction: row`, the main axis runs horizontally. In `column` it runs vertically. Alignment properties work relative to the axis.

exercise.task:
Build two layouts with flexbox. Work in `index.html`.

- `.row` becomes a flex container so its three `.item` children sit side by side.
- Each `.row .item` gets `flex: 1` so they share the width equally.
- `.col` becomes a flex container with `flex-direction: column`.
hints: Flexbox starts with one declaration on the parent, `display: flex`.
The items need `flex: 1` (a rule for `.row .item`), and the column container needs `flex-direction`.

checks.name: .col stacks its items in a column
